name: Outside Snatch Flow — Figure 8 → Tactical Clean → Transverse Lunge → Outside Snatch → Windmill → Snatch → Thruster → Deep Squat Press → Switch Swing
description:
The most overhead-loaded of the Madeleine Conti single-bell flows in the library. A figure-8 entry threads into the rack, a rack-loaded transverse lunge rotates the hips, then the bell goes overhead four different ways — an outside-path snatch, a windmill, a between-the-legs snatch, and two presses that look alike but aren't. Run the whole chain on one side, then the other.

**The flow runs on bell PATH, and the path is not intuitive. Three things to know before you start:**

**1. Inside rack, then outside arc.** Coming out of the transverse lunge you stand up and settle the bell into what Conti calls the **inside rack** — bell threaded up the inside line, elbow tight to the ribs. That landing is not decoration: it is the only position the outside snatch can launch from. From the inside rack the bell drops down and OUT around the working hip on a pendulum arc and rides that arc overhead. It never hikes between the legs. Land the rack sloppy or wide and the outside arc has nowhere to start.

**2. The bell stays racked through the transverse lunge.** It does not swing, it does not drop. The lunge is a rotation *under* a racked load — that's what makes it hard and what makes the inside rack available at the top.

**3. The two presses are opposites.** The thruster (Conti: "viking press") is fast, with leg drive feeding the bell overhead in one motion. The deep squat press (Conti: "long press") has NO leg drive — full deep squat, hold the bottom, stand all the way up, then press strict. Same-looking beats, different engines. Run them the same and the flow loses its point.

A hand-to-hand switch swing hands the bell over and parks it in the hike for the other side. Overhead-heavy and shoulder-hungry — light-to-medium bell, and mind the right shoulder on the snatches, the windmill, and both presses.
flowNotes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side — figure 8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → switch swing — letting each move feed the next, then park the bell in the hike and repeat on the other side. Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell; the bell goes overhead on five of the nine beats, so the load ceiling is set by the weakest overhead position, not the strongest pull. **Mind the right shoulder** — pack it DOWN on every lockout, and bail on the windmill or a press before grinding it. The cleans, snatches, and swing come from the legs and hips, not the arm. The prescription on the reel is 1-2 rounds per side, 8-10 sets, 1 min rest between sets.

flowSequence.notes: Feet wide, chest up, stay low. Weave the bell through the legs in a figure-8 to open the flow — hand off cleanly behind, no rushing.
Out of the last figure-8 pass, thread the bell up the inside path into the rack. Controlled, no momentum yank, no forearm bang.

Bell STAYS racked. Pivot and sweep the trailing leg back and across at an angle, torso rotating open, free arm forward as counterbalance. Drive back to standing and re-settle the bell into a clean rack — the landing position Conti calls the 'inside rack', and it's what sets the path for the snatch that follows.

From the rack, drop the bell down and OUT around the working hip — no hike between the legs — and ride that outside arc straight overhead. Hips drive it, core braced so the torso doesn't twist toward the bell. Punch the hand through to a soft catch.

Stay in the overhead lockout from the snatch. Turn the feet ~45° away from the loaded side, eyes on the bell, hinge and lower the free hand toward the floor with the overhead arm locked. Regress the depth or skip it entirely if the right shoulder complains.

Straight out of the windmill's lockout — lower the bell down the front, hike it BETWEEN the legs, and snap the hips to send it back overhead. Unlike the outside snatch, this one runs the standard between-the-legs path. Punch through, soft catch on the forearm.
Single-arm. Lower to the rack, dip, and drive up so the leg drive feeds the press straight overhead in one motion. Fast and explosive — this is the momentum press. Conti calls it a 'viking press'.

The opposite of the thruster you just did. Lower to the rack, sink to a FULL deep squat and hold the bottom a beat, stand all the way up, and only then press strict overhead. No leg drive into the press — that's the whole contrast, and it's the harder of the two.

Lower the bell, hike it back between the legs and swing it up, releasing at the float point to catch it in the OTHER hand. Then hinge, swing it back down, and park it in the hike on the floor — the bell is now set up for the other side.

tips: This is a FLOW — the nine moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Smooth, controlled transitions are the point.
Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell. Five of the nine beats put the bell overhead, so pick the load your weakest overhead position can hold, not the one your pull can.
The reel's prescription: 1-2 rounds per side, 8-10 sets, 1 min rest between sets. As practice, 1 round per side for 2-3 easy sets is plenty.

**The two presses are deliberately different.** The thruster ('viking press') uses leg drive and is fast; the deep squat press has no leg drive, a full deep bottom, and a strict overhead finish. Run them differently or the flow loses its point.

**Overhead-heavy — the shoulder sets the ceiling.** Outside snatch, windmill, snatch, and both presses all load the shoulder overhead or on a long lever. Pack the shoulder DOWN on every lockout; regress or skip the windmill first if the right shoulder flares.
The transverse lunge is rotational — the bell stays racked and the load fights the twist. It is not a lateral lunge and it is not a curtsy; the pivot and the open torso are the exercise.
Great for overhead stability, rotational control, ballistic skill, grip, and full-body coordination.
